title: impeccable · the Ask surface
question: The roll dealt three compositions for the Ask surface (seed 36013237). The print world is already settled — warm paper, 3px ink borders, hard offset shadows, no radius and no blur — so this choice is structure, not identity. The surface's job is evidence: the Agent is the fourth piece of shipped work, and the Source it cites is the load-bearing element. Lock one.

options.label: The Bench
options.lineage: a printed page, replaced sheet by sheet
options.thesis: An answer is a printed page, not a message — so the surface prints one at a time, at full scale.
options.viewport: No scrollback. The question sets at destination scale across the sheet's largest brick; the answer runs beneath it at reading measure, and a sticky aside — the same panel a Case Study uses for its facts — names every Source the answer stood on. Earlier questions collect as a strip of numbered mono chips along the bottom edge.
options.case: Strongest on the evidence job: the Source aside is permanent furniture rather than a footnote, so grounding is visible before you read a word of the answer.
options.risk: A reader trained on chat will hunt for scrollback before they find the chip strip. The stepper has to read as navigation on first sight.

options.label: The Switchboard
options.thesis: A hiring manager with three minutes does not know what to ask — so the board asks for them.
options.viewport: A board of real questions, each one a ticket that fills with a project's colour as it lifts, exactly like the project tickets on Home. Clicking a ticket opens its answer in place with a horizontal strip of Source cards beneath it. The composer sits under the board for anything not already on it.
options.case: Best first-viewport legibility of the three, and it reuses a primitive the site already owns, so it costs the least new vocabulary.
options.risk: Browse-first framing makes a live Agent look like a canned FAQ — the exact opposite of the evidence job you picked.

options.label: The Transcript
options.lineage: the chat column every AI portfolio ships
options.thesis: The arrangement the reader already knows, executed in this kit without irony.
options.viewport: Question bricks and answer bricks stacked down one column, each answer footed by a Source plate, the composer docked at the bottom as an ink-bordered bar that presses when you send.
options.case: Zero learning cost and the only one of the three that stays comfortable after twenty exchanges. Honest, and honestly the default.
options.risk: It is what every AI portfolio ships, so the Agent reads as a bolted-on widget — and About already promises the opposite: agents that work with a product's own domain 'rather than being bolted on as a separate chat interface.'
